I have to say that there is a certain number of working hours involved, and whenever that amount of hours is used up, that's to say the piece of equipment has been used for such and such a number of hours, it has to go and be officially checked.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Covilo, during your time in the General Staff of the VJ did you ever hear of the plan called "Drina"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO COVILO
utterances.text: No. As of 1992 I was no longer dealing with communications plans and I was no longer privy to any plans for their use.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: Did you, during your service, see any other documents which had to do with this particular plan?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO COVILO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we call up Prosecution Exhibit P1564. It doesn't have --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. Zorko.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we first turn to page 2, both in Serbian and English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You were going to tell us that it doesn't have something, which you didn't complete, Mr. Zorko. What did you want to say, it doesn't have what?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I wanted to say was that it wasn't an MFI'd document, but my microphone was switched off, so ... It's an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: Mr. Covilo --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Or rather, can we have page 2 of both versions on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: I would like to have your comments on what you see on your screen. Is there anything in particular that you note on this page?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO COVILO
utterances.text: Your Honours, Mr. Zorko, what I see is a list of documents pertaining to the communications plan Drina, which was drawn up pursuant to instructions concerning communications. I don't know why. It does have a stamp but it doesn't bear a signature, which it normally would, of both those who handed it over and received it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we turn to page 6 in the B/C/S now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we do that, the witness is telling us by reading from the B/C/S that these are communications items plan of the Drina. We don't see any Drina on the English page and our page doesn't look like it's the first page. It has no heading.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is page 2 in English. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It starts with number 1, Communications Order number 1, 3, which seems to be the same entry in B/C/S. Then number 2, radio communications schematic 1, 1. Looks like it's the same page, but we don't have a heading.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please go to page 1 in both languages in order to see what document we are dealing with. Could we please have page 2 in both next.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We have seen the word "Drina." Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: Mr. Covilo, what can you tell us about the fact that there is no signature on this page?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honours. That calls for speculation. The plan is dated November 1993. Mr. Covilo has already explained to us that from 1992 he would have not been in a position where he would have been privy to such a plan. He has been showed one page of the document and now he is being asked to speculate on how it may or may not have been created.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That is true except that I thought in a previous answer he did refer to the fact that it is unsigned and did try to mention what he makes of that, but was -- may have been interrupted. I'm trying to look -- okay. If you look at page 47, starting at line 7: "Your Honours, Mr. Zorko, what I see is a list of documents pertaining to the communications plan Drina which was drawn up pursuant to instructions concerning communications. I don't know why it does have a stamp but it doesn't bear a signature, which it normally would, of both those who handed it over and received it."

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That was an unsolicited answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes, but what I understand he is now being asked at page 48, line 5, is to explain the fact that there is no signature on the document or to -- well, that's one interpretation of the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The other interpretation is you've told us that it should normally have a signature, what does it mean even if it doesn't have a signature; what is the effect?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Then that's how the question should be framed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Zorko.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. And another thank you goes to my learned friend. I'll more or less repeat my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: Mr. Covilo, what does the fact that there's no signature here tell you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO COVILO
utterances.text: To couch it in the mildest possible terms, it tells me there was no compliance on how communication documents should be compiled. The normal procedure during a hand-over of a document like this would be to have a signature of both the sender and the recipient.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now please be shown page 6 in the B/C/S and page 6 in the English as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: Mr. Covilo, you see a diagram there. It's much clearer in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do I take it we don't have it in the English, this diagram, with the annotations in English?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The diagram should be at English page number 7. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies. This is only the lower part, but we don't have the upper portion of the diagram. We will press on no matter what.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: Mr. Covilo, based on your knowledge, was a communications system like this established in the VJ, and what can you tell us about this diagram?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO COVILO
utterances.text: Your Honours, Mr. Zorko, what I can tell is this: This is a perfectly standard diagram compiled in keeping with the documents setting out the rules for communications system. It's difficult to specify anything else. I'm not sure if this is out of its proper context or whatever, I'm not sure why the Drina plan was drafted, and I certainly had no chance to see for myself whether this communications system specifically ever got off the ground or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Covilo.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm done with this document. Mr. Covilo, we'll be showing you another document. This is an OTP document, P2622, please. Thank you. It's not an MFI'd document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: P?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 2622, Your Honours. Your Honours, we are facing some minor e-court problems right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And what is the nature of --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure if perhaps ...

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the counsel.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: Have you read the document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO COVILO
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: Mr. Covilo, at the time of this document, did the VJ have an evolved command and communications system?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO COVILO
utterances.text: No, there was information support but it didn't have a command and communications system that was evolved.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: Do you know when the VJ eventually developed one?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO COVILO
utterances.text: If memory serves, it wasn't until after 1995. There was an experimental development of the command and communications system. I remember the Assistant Chief of General Staff for communications, information technology, and electronic activity was late Colonel Zugec [Realtime transcript read in error "General Djukic"] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Slow down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sometime after 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But slow down, sir. The interpreter was running at a thousand miles trying to keep up pace with you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I'll try to make sure I don't do that again.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe we are talking about the command and information system and again we have a small problem with the interpretation. I'll repeat my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: If you look at this text, Mr. Covilo, it talks about the development of a command and information system. Is that the system that you had in mind a minute ago?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO COVILO
utterances.text: Yes. Command, control, communication, and reconnaissance.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: All of these are elements of the system you are talking about?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO COVILO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Covilo.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document is no longer required. Thank you. Again intervention, Your Honours, line 51 -- page 51, line 14, General Djukic was mentioned although the witness in fact never mentioned a General Djukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zorko.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the President, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zorko. I'm very sorry. I believe that is corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: Mr. Covilo, do you know that at one point in time the FRY introduced or imposed sanctions on the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO COVILO
utterances.text: Yes. All the people of the FRY knew about that because it was something that was published in the media.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: Do you know about the exact point in time the sanctions were imposed, and when did they take effect?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO COVILO
utterances.text: I believe sometime in late 1994. I hope I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Covilo. What about this very fact, the fact that the sanctions were imposed? Did that in any way affect the existing communication lines to Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO COVILO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: In what way? Please explain.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO COVILO
utterances.text: I remember a collegium meeting with the assistant commander of the General Staff for the communication, information technology, and electronic activity. When he came back from a meeting with the Chief of the General Staff, he conveyed an order to the chief of the communications administration. The order said that all communication was to cease to the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: Just to be perfectly clear, whose order was that about severing communication lines?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO COVILO
utterances.text: The chief of the General Staff, Mr. Momcilo Perisic, issued an order to the assistant, General Obradovic, the assistant of the chief of the communication, information technology, and electronic activity administration, and he issued the order or conveyed to Mr. Zelkovic, the chief of the communication administration, and who Perisic got the order from, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, very much. Your Honours, I have no further questions for this witness. This might be a convenient time for our break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. It is indeed. We'll take a break and come back at quarter to 6.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Mr. Covilo, good afternoon. My name is Barney Thomas. I'm a lawyer with the Prosecution. I'm sure my friend Mr. Zorko has explained this to you already but what happens now, sir, is I have an opportunity to ask you some questions about the testimony that you have given this afternoon. I can tell you now that we won't be keeping you long, sir. I don't have a lot of questions for you. But what I do ask is that, please, you listen to my questions carefully, answer only the question that I have asked you. If there is anything about my question which you do not understand, please say so and I'll rephrase my question or otherwise deal with the difficulty that we have. Is that clear enough, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO COVILO
utterances.text: It is, thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Sir, at the beginning of your testimony this afternoon, you spoke about how you were sent to the area of Mostar to assist in the reinstatement of PTT systems and several municipalities. Do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO COVILO
utterances.text: Yes. To the Bileca area specifically, not Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: The transcript isn't quite complete, but you referred to being sent to Bileca, Trebinje, and Gacko to work on the PTT systems. Are those municipalities correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO COVILO
utterances.text: Yes. Trebinje, Bileca, Nevesinje, and Gacko.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: At the time that you travelled and worked in those municipalities, those had already been taken by the VRS, hadn't they?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO COVILO
utterances.text: That's right. When I arrived, the JNA was there and later the VRS came.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Later on in your testimony, sir, you spoke about radio relay communications, and I wish to explore that issue with you just for a few moments. We know from your testimony that at the time of the JNA withdrawal, there were radio relay stations located throughout each of the republics; well, specifically, Croatia, Bosnia, and Serbia; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO COVILO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And in talking about the ability of the VRS to conduct its communications without needing to rely on VJ communications structure, you mentioned that there would not be a need for the VRS to use any radio relay stations that were located in Serbia. Do you recall that statement, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO COVILO
utterances.text: Yes. It had involved infrastructure of both the stationary communication hubs and centres. And a total of five command facilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now, the ability of one unit to communicate with another is dependent upon, amongst other things, whether or not they have a direct line of sight to a radio relay station, and the range of that radio relay station; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO COVILO
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. In terms of radio relay, in addition to an open line of sight, the distance should not exceed 50 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Would you accept, sir, that depending on where a unit of the VRS was garrisoned, radio relay communication, for example, with the Main Staff of the VRS, may have to be routed through communication centres located on the territory of the FRY? Would you accept that that was sometimes necessary?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO COVILO
utterances.text: As far as I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just a second, Mr. Covilo. Yes, Mr. Zorko.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm looking at the question and I see a rather broad approach, asking the witness to speculate. The witness is being asked to speculate because we don't know where specifically this unit that my learned friend is referring to is supposed to be located. We don't know about the distance involved. I think this question can hardly be answered without speculating.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: The witness has stated, sir, that there would be no need for VRS units to resort to FRY radio relay stations, and I'm asking him whether he can exclude the possibility of that being necessary, depending on the location of a unit. I'm asking him to qualify his earlier unequivocal statement, sir, or at least giving him the opportunity to qualify his earlier unequivocal statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Except in that if he has already said there would be no need, he has said there would be no need. Maybe you might confront him with a specific situation where it did happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I can do that, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: General, where were the Eastern Bosnian Corps of the VRS garrisoned?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO COVILO
utterances.text: Your Honours, Mr. Prosecutor, I'm not fully familiar with the deployment of the forces of the VRS. As far as I know, that location would be somewhere in the Bijeljina sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Let's deal with Bijeljina for the moment. Where was the Main Staff of the VRS located?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO COVILO
utterances.text: As far as I know, in the general Han Pijesak area.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And which was the main communications hub that was used by the VRS Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO COVILO
utterances.text: The main hub was at Veliki Zep.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: If the Main Staff of the VRS wished to communicate with the eastern -- no, if the Main Staff of the VRS wished to communicate with the unit garrisoned at Bijeljina, what would be the radio relay route?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zorko.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, again I think the witness is being asked to speculate as to how a certain unit, in this case the Main Staff of the VRS, would establish a line of communication with another unit. The witness was never a member of the VRS and he is being asked to address matters that he is not directly familiar with. Therefore, I think this is another case of asking the witness to speculate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: With respect, Your Honour, the witness has been called, amongst other things, to talk about the location of the radio relay communications centres, how they operated before the break-up, where they were positioned after the break-up. He has given testimony that they could -- that the VRS could communicate without resorting to any communications centres in the FRY, I'm being very specific now of giving him an example of radio relay communications between the hub of the Main Staff of the VRS at Veliki Zep and Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zorko.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise, Your Honours, if I may be of assistance. Mr. Covilo was never involved with VRS communications systemS, and my learned friend is asking him to answer a question that directly addresses something that he could only ever know if he was involved with the systems. The witness is still being asked to speculate from where I stand, therefore I stand by my objection, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You see, I hear what you say, but the problem is that Mr. Covilo said the VRS -- and I'm relying on Mr. Thomas's characterisation of the evidence, I don't remember this from -- independently. He says the VRS would not need, would never need to use the FRY communication system, which would be different from saying they did not use it. So if he says they would never need and he claims to have certain knowledge of why they wouldn't need to do so, on that basis assuming that you are nodding of the head together with madam next to you, suggests that you agree with that characterization of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me just rule formally for the record. Then the objection is overruled.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Mr. Covilo, let me just repeat my question for you. If the Main Staff of the VRS wish to communicate with a unit garrisoned at Bijeljina, what would be the radio relay route?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO COVILO
utterances.text: Your Honours, Mr. Prosecutor, I'd be hard put to remember the exact radio relay route. Nevertheless, what I can tell you is this: Take any route you like along radio relay line. One could set up two or three radio relay stations, meaning if you want to have a line from point A to point B, the distance could be as much as 150 kilometres. Now, between Bijeljina and Veliki Zep, I don't think the distance is that much.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Would you accept, sir, that communications between Bijeljina and Veliki Zep pass through the Cer communications centre? Do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO COVILO
utterances.text: I really don't know, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Well, see, the difficulty, Mr. Covilo, is that you gave what appeared to be an unequivocal statement, that statement being that they would not need to resort to any radio communications or radio relay towers on the territory of Serbia. So all I'm doing, sir, to be fair, is I'm giving you the opportunity to qualify that statement, if you wish. Would you accept that it's entirely possible, given the location of units, that they needed to resort to radio relay communications passing through radio relay stations situated on the territory of the FRY? Would you accept that as a possibility?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO COVILO
utterances.text: Yes, I would. I'm in no position to rule that out, the fact that there was a simpler way of establishing a line of communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: So if there was testimony to that effect from other Defence witnesses, you wouldn't challenge that testimony?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO COVILO
utterances.text: I don't see why I would. I really don't know what sort of communication line was set up. I do stand by the fact that -- which I said before, and that's that had I been a VRS commander, I would have easily organised a communications system of the VRS without resorting to the hubs in Serbia, and of course there may have been simpler routes of doing this rather than going through Cer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: So do I understand your position to be, sir, that in theory it could be done? In other words, communications could be established without needing to route them through Cer or through Crni Vrh or through Strazbenica but you can't say with any degree of certainty whether in practice those radio relay stations were indeed avoided? Is that a fair characterization of your position?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zorko.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I still maintain that the witness is called to speculate, and I think that witness answered on page 59, line 23, that he didn't really know ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you done, Mr. Zorko?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I am, Your Honour. That's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Sir, at page 60, line 13, the witness has said: "I don't really know what sort of communication line was set up. I do stand by the fact that which I said before --" which he didn't say, but -- "which I said before and that's that had I been a VRS commander, I would have easily organised a communications system of the VRS without resorting to the hubs in Serbia. And of course there may have been simpler routes of doing this rather than going through Cer." So given that answer, sir, what I'm trying to do now is to get him to commit to a position. If his position is that his answer is limited to what could be done in theory and that he can't really speak about what was actually done by the VRS commanders in practice, then that's something we need to know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I think that would be allowed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Prosecutor, there did exist a technical possibility for communications to be set up only on the side of the VRS, and there also existed the technical possibility to use communications hubs of the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And as far as whether the VRS commanders actually used communications hubs on the territory of the FRY, is it true that you can't tell us? You can't be certain yourself whether they did or they didn't? Is that your position?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO COVILO
utterances.text: Yes, that's my position. At this time I was not privy to the communications system used either by the Army of Yugoslavia or the army -- or the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Mr. Covilo, thank you. Your Honours, that concludes my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Thomas. Mr. Zorko, any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to make a clarification for the transcript. In -- on page 62, line 3, you said that you were not privy to the communications system used either by the Army of Yugoslavia or by the Army of Republika Srpska. Is really the Army of Yugoslavia of what you have in mind? I wasn't sure whether that was a mistake.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO COVILO
utterances.text: Yes, the army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: Can you explain what you meant by this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO COVILO
utterances.text: What I meant was that at that time I was not a communications planner and it was not within my duties to go into any details and to see where the various radio relay routes had been organised, and to see whether possibly any of the communication hubs was placed at the disposal of someone for a stretch of these routes. What I can tell you is that at no point in time was access or entry to the communications system of the VJ allowed, which doesn't mean to say that a communications hub could not have been used as an intermediary radio relay station to ensure communication that went further. In that case, a hub would be used as a passageway, really, like in the case of somebody being allowed to use someone else's meadow.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just one question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: When you say at that time -- you say, What I meant was that at that time I was not a communications planner. Which time specifically are you referring to here?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO COVILO
utterances.text: I'm referring to the period starting with August of 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Until?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO COVILO
utterances.text: Until the end of my professional service with the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If you could just remind us, when was that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO COVILO
utterances.text: I don't understand, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: When was the end of your professional service with the Army of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO COVILO
utterances.text: In 1999 I was assigned or transferred to the Ministry of Defence to work within the PTT system as director of the sector for defence preparations. And in December 2003, I retired.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. So until December 2003, that's the short answer?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO COVILO
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, then, Mr. Covilo. This brings us to the conclusion of your -- I beg your pardon. I am sorry, we haven't reached that stage. Any questions arising from the questions by the Bench? Mr. Zorko?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: No, sir, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then that brings us to the end of your testimony for the day. Thank you so much for taking the time off to come and testify at the tribunal. You are now excused, you may stand down, and please travel well back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I thank the Trial Chamber for allowing me to give my testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Zorko.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to give the floor to Mr. Guy-Smith. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that would be the concluding the testimony of those witnesses that we have for the balance of this week. Our next witness is scheduled to testify on Monday. We do not have further witnesses for this week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The next witness will be Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, can somebody help me --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can somebody help me. I don't seem to have the latest court schedule with me. Is Courtroom II operational? Will it be operational by Monday, or is it still not?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether it is or is not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Microphone for you, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether it is or is not. I've been given mixed messages on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Registrar. I'm advised we are in Courtroom I next week, in the morning. So we stand adjourned to Monday morning on the 20th of September at 9.00 in Courtroom I. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 20th day of September, 2010, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.08 p.m.
